latest_teacher_action.diagnosis: The generated image preserved one checkered lion, one croissant, and the raccoons-to-the-left-of-croissant spatial relation, but failed to make the raccoons clearly present and countable as seven, failed to show the lion visibly chasing them, and failed to bind the stone material to the croissant. The next prompt must make seven raccoons the central countable group, arrange a clear chase direction from lion to raccoons, and describe the croissant as a rock-textured stone object rather than an ordinary pastry.
expected_improvement: Seven raccoons should be explicitly visible, individually separated, and countable with no extra raccoons.
The lion should read as actively chasing the raccoons by being behind them, facing them, and posed in motion toward them while the raccoons flee away.
The single croissant should be recognized as made of stone through carved rock texture and hard stone surface cues.
Previously passed constraints should remain stable: exactly one checkered lion, exactly one croissant, raccoons left of croissant, and no extra required objects.
preserve_constraints: Keep exactly one lion visible in the image.
Keep the lion checkered, with the checkered pattern bound only to the lion.
Keep exactly one croissant visible in the image.
Keep all raccoons positioned to the left of the single croissant.
Do not include any additional lions, raccoons, or croissants beyond the required counts.

previous_plan_error.details: The previous prompt described the raccoons as a group and asked for countability, but it did not force a strong, staged layout where all seven raccoons dominate the scene as separate instances. The chase relation was too abstract and could be missed if the lion was only oriented toward them. The croissant material clause was also weak because a croissant may default to pastry unless the stone material is made visually unmistakable.
previous_plan_error.error_source: Prompt under-specified visual salience for the seven raccoons, the chase action, and the stone material binding.

latest_teacher_action.regeneration_strategy: Use a simple side-view composition with a clear left-to-right layout: seven separate raccoons in the middle-left, the single checkered lion behind them on the far left lunging toward them, and the single stone croissant on the far right. Make each raccoon fully visible with gaps between bodies. Make the chase relation explicit by showing the lion running after the raccoons and the raccoons fleeing away from the lion. Bind stone material directly to the croissant using carved rock texture and hard stone surface language.
regression_risks: The model may reduce the raccoon count or merge raccoons if they overlap, so the prompt must demand seven separate full-body raccoons with visible gaps and no extras.
The lion's checkered attribute could be lost while focusing on the raccoons, so the prompt must keep one visibly checkered lion.
The croissant may revert to an ordinary pastry, so the prompt must repeatedly bind stone material to the croissant only.
The spatial relation could regress if the croissant is placed among the animals, so the prompt must keep every raccoon to the left of the croissant.
repair_constraints: Show exactly seven raccoons, all present as separate visible animals, with gaps between them and no overlapping or merged bodies.
Depict the single lion actively chasing the raccoons: the lion is behind the raccoons, facing them, running or lunging toward them, while the raccoons are ahead of the lion fleeing away.
Make the croissant a stone croissant: one croissant-shaped object with carved rock texture and hard stone material, not a soft pastry.
Keep all seven raccoons to the left of the single stone croissant.
Keep exactly one checkered lion and exactly one croissant; include no extra lions, raccoons, or croissants.
